investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-14T22:36–22:44Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and no other nodes satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This prevents the eval runner from reaching the createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) and therefore no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is ever written, causing all three remote-agent checks to fail. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the 2 kata/peerpods-capable nodes are occupied by existing agents or workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes in the 6-node cluster satisfy, meaning the schedulable pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster capacity.

[Possible] Leaked or zombie remote agent VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup: if previous probe runs left agents running, they may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, reducing available capacity for new probes.

[Possible] Cluster autoscaler not configured or not triggered for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes: the scheduler message shows preemption found no victims and could not help, suggesting no scale-out path was available within the scheduling window.
[Lower confidence] Temporary spike in concurrent remote agent usage by other workloads coinciding with the eval window, transiently exhausting the fixed VM pool.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-14T22:36–22:44Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and no other nodes satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This prevents the eval runner from reaching the createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) and therefore no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is ever written, causing all three remote-agent checks to fail. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM workload: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption path was available. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval probe never received any response, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run (2026-07-14T22:41:38Z–22:44:08Z), 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported it as fully consumed, and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both node sets. The pod remained Unschedulable for 143–149 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
